audio_script_it:
Buongiorno, benvenuti al Morning Briefing di Price Alert.

Il Nikkei ha chiuso in rialzo dello 0.97%, Shanghai in calo dello 0.33%. Questo suggerisce un'apertura mista per i mercati europei.

Nella seduta precedente, l'S&P 500 ha chiuso in rialzo dello 0.80%, il VIX è sceso del 3.11%. L'oro si mantiene sopra i 4720 dollari l'oncia, in rialzo dello 0.37%. Il petrolio Brent è salito dello 0.25%.

La situazione geopolitica rimane tesa, con l'attenzione rivolta alle possibili conseguenze dell'aumento delle tensioni nel Medio Oriente.

I dati macroeconomici recenti mostrano un'inflazione core PCE negli USA del 3.0% su base annua. La BCE ha mantenuto invariati i tassi di interesse.

Mentre le borse mondiali osservano la consueta pausa festiva, i riflettori restano accesi sul comparto digitale, dove Bitcoin ha chiuso in rialzo dello 0.17% a 77,585 dollari e Ethereum è salito dello 0.28% a 2,317 dollari.

[{'bitcoin': 'Bitcoin si mantiene sopra i settantasettemila dollari, con una variazione del -0.11%. Flussi ETF in aumento con un inflow di 223.3 milioni di dollari.'}, {'altcoins': 'Tra le altcoin, Ethereum guadagna lo 0.28% a 2317 dollari, Solana +1.12% a 86.40 dollari e BNB +0.38% a 637.55 dollari.'}, {'sentiment': 'Il Fear & Greed Index è a 31, in zona Fear.'}]

Grazie per aver ascoltato il nostro podcast finanziario. Per domani, tenete d'occhio l'andamento dei mercati europei e americani, con particolare attenzione agli indici PMI e ai dati sull'inflazione. Un saluto da Price Alert, arrivederci alla prossima puntata. Grazie per l'attenzione e a domani!
audio_script_en:
Good morning, welcome to the Price Alert Morning Briefing. 
  While traditional markets observe their holiday break, the spotlight remains on digital assets which are open 24/7. 
  At the last close, Asia wrapped up the week with the Nikkei up 0.97% at 59,716 and Shanghai down 0.33% at 4,079.90. 
  This sets a neutral tone for European and US markets, had they been open.

  Focusing on the previous close for Western markets: 
  The S&P 500 was up 0.80% at 7,165.08, VIX dropped 3.11% to 18.71, and the Dollar Index declined 0.29% to 98.51. 
  Gold holds above $4,500/oz at $4,722.30/oz up 0.37%, and oil edged up 0.25% to $105.33.

  In geopolitics and macro, 
  Underlying inflation remains on track for Bank of Japan rate normalization. 
  The ECB signs agreements to facilitate digital euro payments. 
  Geopolitical tensions, particularly around the Strait of Hormuz, continue to influence market sentiment.

  Shifting focus to digital assets, 
  Bitcoin is up 0.17% at $77,585. 
  Ethereum is up 0.28% at $2,317, Solana up 1.12% at $86.40, and BNB up 0.38% at $637.55. 
  The Fear & Greed Index stands at 31, indicating fear.

Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets. Bitcoin is trading at seventy-seven thousand five hundred forty-nine dollars, down zero point one one percent. The ETF daily net inflow is two hundred twenty-three point three million dollars.

In the altcoin space, Ethereum is up zero point two eight percent to two thousand three hundred seventeen dollars. Solana is up one point one two percent to eighty-six point four dollars. Binance Coin is up zero point three eight percent to six hundred thirty-seven point five five dollars.

The Fear & Greed Index is at thirty-one, still in the Fear category. Overall, it's a mixed bag in the crypto markets today.

Thanks for tuning in and we'll see you tomorrow. Have a great day and goodbye from Price Alert.

articles.title: The Strait of Hormuz energy crisis shows the EU’s carbon pricing is the right approach
articles.snippet: The Strait of Hormuz energy crisis shows the EU’s carbon pricing is the right approach Expert comment thilton.drupal 24 April 2026 The current crisis shows that Europe must transition to renewables to reduce its dependency on volatile fossil fuels. This week’s AccelerateEU plan rightly reaffirms that goal. The global energy crisis caused by the closure of the Strait of Hormuz has demonstrated the vulnerability of relying on fossil fuels. Even if the Strait reopens in the near future, traffic flows are likely to be lower, with insurance premiums remaining high and Iran monitoring shipping through the Strait. QatarEnergy’s production facilities also remain damaged, impacting the supply of liquified natural gas (LNG) from the world’s largest exporter. As a result, energy prices are projected

articles.title: Airwaves of Power: Why the Pentagon Should Shift to a Commercial-First Spectrum Model
articles.snippet: The U.S. military is firing million-dollar missiles at Iranian drones that cost a tiny fraction as much — a striking example of the kind of overmatch modern warfare punishes.The Department of Defense’s approach to electromagnetic spectrum policy follows a similar logic, occupying prime mid-band frequencies for vital but relatively low-throughput national security uses — including radars, satellite communications, navigation, and electronic warfare — even as those same bands could generate much larger commercial, allied, and strategic returns.The Pentagon understandably views spectrum through a national security lens, but the current allocation reflects less strategic optimization than a legacy of policy choices The post Airwaves of Power: Why the Pentagon Should Shift to a Commercial-First

articles.title: Book launch: World War Trade: Conflict, Containment, and the Emergent World Trading Order
articles.snippet: Globalization is not dying. It is being rebuilt. When the United States and China weaponized trade in 2025, many feared the collapse of the global economy. Markets plunged, supply chains fractured, and policymakers spoke openly of economic warfare. But the collapse never came. In his new book, World War Trade, published by the Centre for Economic Policy Research, Richard Baldwin argues that the real story is not the conflict between superpowers but how the rest of the world responded. Through quiet restraint, strategic adaptation, and a wave of new trade agreements, countries representing the…

articles.title: IEA’s Birol Says Iran War Will Permanently Cut Into Future Oil Demand
articles.snippet: International Energy Agency chief Fatih Birol says the Iran war has permanently changed the fossil fuel industry and will accelerate a shift toward renewables, nuclear power and electrification at the expense of oil demand. That is a bold claim in the middle of an oil crisis that has Brent trading above $105 a barrel and physical supply still constrained. Birol told The Guardian that the damage to confidence in fossil fuel security is permanent, and that countries exposed to the Strait of Hormuz disruption will rethink how much geopolitical risk…

articles.title: JPMorgan Says Oil Prices Still Have Further to Rise
articles.snippet: JPMorgan says oil prices still have further to rise because the market has not yet forced enough demand out of the system to offset the supply loss from the Iran war. Global oil supply disruptions reached 9.1 million barrels per day in March and climbed to 13.7 million barrels per day in April, according to JPMorgan’s Natasha Kaneva. The first relief valve, spare capacity, has not worked because supply from Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates remains cut off. Inventories are being pulled instead.
